title: R-(+)-limonene response in Penicillium: a publisher-table audit
question: Which metabolic and signaling responses to terpene exposure are reproducible, and which depend on cellular context or a specific target?

sources.title: Zhang et al., R-(+)-limonene biotransformation by Penicillium digitatum (2020)
Publisher Data Sheet 1, including Table S7

claims.text: The source study sampled Penicillium digitatum DSM 62840 after 12 hours with 840 mg/L R-(+)-limonene and compared it with an untreated 12-hour arm; it also sampled an untreated zero-hour arm.
claims.limitation: The zero-hour arm is not time matched and should not substitute for the 12-hour untreated comparison.

claims.text: The publisher workbook Table S7 has 58 unique nonblank gene rows. In the time-matched expression columns, 31 are higher and 27 lower after limonene exposure.
claims.limitation: These are directions in author-provided expression values, not independently estimated differential-expression calls.

claims.text: Only 10 of the 58 rows have an explicit P450 or CYP label in either the supplied NR or KEGG annotation text (8 in NR, 6 in KEGG, with overlap).
claims.limitation: A text match neither proves P450 function for labeled genes nor excludes it for unlabeled genes; the table cannot identify a binding target.

claims.text: Table S7 does not include per-gene adjusted p values or replicate-level measurements, so its reported candidate significance cannot be independently audited from this workbook.
claims.limitation: The paper describes a count-based differential-expression method, but the necessary per-gene statistics are absent from this supplementary table.

claims.text: The article reports 4,148 DEGs for the limonene-treated versus untreated 12-hour comparison and discusses candidate P450 involvement in limonene biotransformation.
claims.limitation: The count is author reported; this notebook does not reproduce it from raw reads or establish a causal enzyme.

claims.text: Reprocess PRJNA608617 raw reads with pinned reference and gene annotation, inspect biological replicates and batch, and fit a count-based model for the time-matched contrast.
claims.limitation: Raw-read reanalysis has not been run in this project.

claims.text: Investigate candidate enzymes through sequence/domain annotation and chemical-genetic or biochemical assays, then compare compatible pathway responses across independently processed terpene cohorts with explicit organism, dose, time, and chemical identity.
claims.limitation: Current expression and annotation evidence does not demonstrate cross-study replication or target dependence.
